info.title: worker-service
info.description:
The API for workers: lasting agents, each living on one host, run in sessions. Hosts send a heartbeat every 30 seconds, which keeps them `connected` and says what they offer. Clients read state and issue commands. Every route under `/fleet` needs the stage's bearer token.

Commands and reports go by WebSocket at `socketUrl` alone: a host connects with `?hostId=<id>` and the stage's token as `Authorization: Bearer`, a page with `?ticket=<one-time ticket>` from `createSocketTicket`. What goes up is a `SocketInbound` (`report`, `ping`), and what comes down a `SocketOutbound`: a host's sockets get each `command` as it is queued, and a host's socket, once open, every command still pending for it; every viewer gets each `worker` as it changes, `lines` as they arrive and the `host` on each heartbeat. A command stays queued until a report names it, so a dropped socket loses nothing: it is replayed on the next.

No body carries the server's time: a response's `Date` header is when it was made, and so when a host's `status` was computed.

workers.description: Workers on the host and what each is doing. One not named is unchanged.

lines.description: Transcript lines not yet sent on a socket that took them.

commandResults.description: One per command taken since it was last reported. A reported command is delivered, and is neither pushed again nor replayed to a socket that connects.

tokens.description: Running token totals of sessions whose count has grown since it was last reported.

SocketReport.description: Host to service, the only way a host reports: whenever something changes, and in full (every worker, every line and result not yet sent) whenever its socket connects. Pushed on to viewers. Idempotent: lines by (`workerId`, `seq`), results by `commandId`. Does not count as a heartbeat. A socket message is at most 128 KB, sent in frames of 32 KB at most, so lines that would not fit go in the reports after it.

id.description: Assigned by the service when the worker is created.

state.description: `idle`: no session running. `working`: its session is taking a turn (from Claude Code's `system` `init` to its `result`). `waiting`: its session is running and between turns. `interrupted`: a session the service started is not running, and was not stopped (a crash, a restart, or a session it does not know).

sessionId.description: The session running, or null for none.

tasks.description: Background tasks and subagents its session has open, as Claude Code's latest `background_tasks_changed` lists them, whether or not a turn is running; 0 once its session ends. Absent from a host that does not say, read as 0.

told.description: Whether the turn running, or the last one, began with a message the host delivered (its echo came back in that turn), rather than by itself, as a turn a background task's end begins does. Absent from a host that does not say, read as unknown.

workerId.description: Assigned by the service when the worker is created.

sessionId.description: Assigned by the service when it queues the session's `start`.

seq.description: Deduplicated by (`workerId`, `seq`), so resending is safe.

from.description: `instruction`: a message sent to the worker.

text.description: Kept whole up to 65536 characters, and past that cut rather than refused, so the rest of its report is not lost with it. A text cut short, by its host to fit a socket message or here, ends `… [cut: N of M characters]`: N kept of the M there were.

commandId.description: On an `instruction` line that is a command's text as the session took it (a `message`, a `start`'s first message, an `interrupt`'s text): that command's id. Absent on any other line.

ok.description: False when the host could not do the command.

error.description: Why not, when `ok` is false, in the host's words.

taken.description: `false` with `ok` true: a command with text, written to its worker's session but not yet taken by it. The command is off the queue (`written`), and its host reports it once more, `ok` true once the session takes it, false if it never will. Absent or true: settled.

workerId.description: Assigned by the service when the worker is created.

sessionId.description: Assigned by the service when it queues the session's `start`.

inputTokens.description: Input tokens not read from or written to the prompt cache.

cacheCreationInputTokens.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache.

cacheReadInputTokens.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache.

SessionTokensReport.description: A session's running total of tokens so far, not what was used since the last report. The service keeps the highest of each count reported for the session, so a total sent again, or late, never adds twice.

readAt.description: When the session's stream said it: its `rate_limit_event`'s time.

allOf.description: The weekly window; absent when the event did not carry it.

UsageReport.description: The account's usage, when a session's stream has said it since the last report.

utilization.description: How much of the window's allowance is used, 0 to 1 (1 is all of it).

resetsAt.description: When the window starts again from 0.

UsageWindowReport.description: The 5-hour window; absent when the event did not carry it.

SocketPing.description: Either side's keep-alive: API Gateway closes a socket idle for 10 minutes.

CommandPush.description: To every socket of the command's host, the moment it is queued; and to a host's socket once it is open, every command still pending for that host, oldest first. That replay follows the first message the host sends on it (its full report on connecting), since API Gateway takes no post to a socket still in `$connect`, and leaves out commands that message reports. A command is pending until a report names it, or until it is withdrawn; a host may see one more than once, and knows it by `id`.

context.description: Files to write into the worker's own Claude Code folder before it starts, replacing the last context's: `skills/...` as files, and a `CLAUDE.md` after the host's own rules. Absent, the last context and documents written stand.

documents.description: Written after `context`, as it is, each with its own files and its `CLAUDE.md` after the one before; they replace the last start's. No two write the same file under `skills/`. Only with a `context`; absent with one, there are none.

contextUrl.description: Present when the whole context is too large for a socket message: the path of `getSessionContext` for this session. A host reads it, with the stage's token, and writes what it answers in place of `context` and `documents`, which then hold only what fitted. A host that cannot read it writes them.

env.description: Set in the session's environment: the addresses of the services it is given. Never a secret.

credentials.description: The services the session is given, by name, as kept on record. Their tokens are in `secrets`.

ownCredentials.description: Of `credentials`, those the worker was given a token of its own for, read in place of the shared one.

secrets.description: The tokens of `credentials`, by variable, read as the command is pushed to the host's socket and never stored, so a listed or replayed command holds none and a rotated secret reaches the next start. The host writes them to a file in the worker's folder that only it can read, and the session's environment is set from that file, never from a command line.

title.description: What the worker named itself for its work, with `setWorkerTitle`, or the person with `renameWorker`. Kept across sessions; null until one is given. Unlike `name`, it names nothing on its host.

label.description: A short tag given when it was made or with `renameWorker`, shown beside its name. Null for none.

item.description: The work item it was started on, as given when it was made; null for none.

role.description: The role it was made from, as given when it was made; null for one made without.

createdBy.description: The `claimed-by` header of the `createWorker` call that made it, unverified. Null when it had none.

whenDone.description: What becomes of the worker once it says it is `done`: `keep`, it stays and a message starts it again; `stop`, its session is stopped; `retire`, it is stopped and retired, as by `retireWorker`. On `review`, `stop` and `retire` both only stop its session, so a send-back can still start it again.

documents.description: What each session is given after `global`, by key.

credentials.description: The services each session is given, by name; null for the stage's defaults. Never a token, nor whether one was the caller's own.

state.description: `idle`: has a home and no live session. `working`, `waiting`: a live session, in a turn or between turns, as its host last reported it (`working` too from the moment a `start` or a message is queued). `interrupted`: its session ended without a stop, and it can be resumed. `retired`: no longer on the team; its home folder is kept on the host.

id.description: Assigned by the service when it queues the session's `start`.

session.description: The live session, or null for none.

reportedAt.description: When its host last reported a change to it; null until its host first reports it.

status.description: What it is doing, as its host sees its turns and as it last said. `working`: a turn of its, or a background task or subagent it started, is running. `idle`: its session is live and neither is, as after it replied; this never needs the person. `waiting`: it said with `setWorkerStatus` that it needs the person, and stays so until the person messages it (a turn it begins by itself does not end it). `review`: its change is submitted to approval-service, said by the worker or by approval-service, and it waits on the reviewer until the change ships or is sent back. `done`: it finished what it was made for, or its change shipped. `review` and `done` are kept once its session ends, and no turn changes them; only a message from the person, or `setWorkerStatus`, does. Otherwise null without a live session. Only `waiting` should notify the person.

summary.description: One line it, or approval-service, last said with `setWorkerStatus`: what it is doing, while `waiting` what it needs from the person. Cleared by a message from the person.

headline.description: A few words said with its `summary` and gone with it, for a list of workers. Null when none was given.

saidAt.description: When `summary` was said; null when there is none.

activity.description: What its latest transcript line says it was doing, and when: a Bash call's description (never its command), another tool's name and target (`Edit src/fleet.ts`, `Agent <its description>`), or the first line of a reply. Never what the person said. Show whichever of it and `summary` is newer, by `at` and `saidAt`. Null until it has done something.

tasks.description: Background tasks and subagents its live session has open, as its host last reported; 0 without one.

told.description: Whether its live session's current or last turn began with a message delivered to it (the person's, or a brief), rather than by itself, as a turn a background task's end begins does; so `idle` after a turn that was told is a reply. Null without a live session, or when its host has not said.

delivery.description: `queued`: not yet reported by the host. `written`: its text is in the worker's session, which has not yet taken it (it takes it at its next step); a session that ends first makes it `rejected`. `withdrawn`: never to be sent, because it went unreported for 300 seconds (`create` and `retire` excepted) or its worker was force-stopped. `done` / `rejected`: the host reported it, done (a text: taken) or not.

post.summary: Keep the host connected, and say what it offers
post.description: Liveness and what the host offers, nothing more: commands come down the host's socket at `socketUrl`, and reports go up it. The host chooses its id; the first heartbeat from an id registers it. Only a heartbeat keeps a host `connected`.

requestBody.description: What the host is and offers.

get.description: Every host that has sent a heartbeat since it was last deregistered with `deleteHost`, however long it has been `lost`. With `status`, only the hosts with one of those statuses.

schema.description: Comma-separated, any of `connected`, `disconnected`, `lost`.

parameters.description: Comma-separated, any of `connected`, `disconnected`, `lost`.
parameters.name: status

delete.description: Deletes the host's record, which is how a host leaves `listHosts`. Its workers, their transcripts and the commands sent to them stay on record, and its workers read as on a `lost` host. The next heartbeat from this id registers it again, and its socket is sent whatever is still queued for it.

get.description: Every role a worker can be made from, highest `priority` first. A stage starts with `planner`, `reviewer`, `conflict`, `investigator`, `judge` and `implementer`, as their callers made them before roles; one written with `createRole` or `updateRole` is served as written.

post.summary: Ask for a worker in a role, to start when usage and a host allow
post.description: Records the request `waiting`, then admits what it can at once. A request starts once both usage windows read under 90% (from a reading under 15 minutes old, or one whose window has since reset) and a connected host carrying its `labels` has a free slot; of those waiting, the highest role `priority` first, then the oldest. Admission runs when a request is made and on every host's heartbeat, every 30 seconds while any host is connected, which is when a host's capacity and usage are next known. A reading older than that, of a window not since reset, still admits one request at a time while both windows read under 70%: one starts once none has since that reading, or none in the last 15 minutes, so the worker it starts gives the next reading. Admitted, the worker is made from its role as `createWorker` with `role` would, with this request's id as its own and a name of the service's choosing (`<role>-<first 8 of its id>`), placed on a host of the service's choosing; `workerId` names it. A request names no host or worker name.

schema.description: Who is making the worker: a person's name, or a service's own, such as `approval-service`. Recorded as `createdBy`, as said and not checked, since every caller holds the same token.

parameters.description: Who is making the worker: a person's name, or a service's own, such as `approval-service`. Recorded as `createdBy`, as said and not checked, since every caller holds the same token.
parameters.name: claimed-by

requestBody.description: What kind of worker, and what it is for.

201.description: Recorded, and `started` if it was admitted at once.

400.description: The request failed validation, the stage has no such role, neither it nor its role has a brief, a credential is not one this stage has, or a token is for a service the worker would not be given.

503.description: No API token is configured, or a token of its own could not be kept.

get.description: Those `waiting`, in the order they would start, each with why it waits. With `all=true`, every one, the waiting first in that order and then the rest newest first. A request starts once both usage windows read under 90% (from a reading under 15 minutes old, or one whose window has since reset) and a connected host carrying its `labels` has a free slot; of those waiting, the highest role `priority` first, then the oldest. Admission runs when a request is made and on every host's heartbeat, every 30 seconds while any host is connected, which is when a host's capacity and usage are next known. A reading older than that, of a window not since reset, still admits one request at a time while both windows read under 70%: one starts once none has since that reading, or none in the last 15 minutes, so the worker it starts gives the next reading.

post.summary: Stop a worker's session, or force it idle
post.description: Queues a `stop`; the session ends and the worker is `idle` once its host reports doing it. When its host is `lost` or deregistered, and so cannot be told, or with `force: true`, the session is ended and the worker `idle` at once, and everything queued for it but `create` is withdrawn; nothing is sent. If its host later reports that session still running, it is sent a `stop`. A caller need not send `force`: the service decides it from the host.

put.summary: Say whether the worker needs the person, is in review or done, and what on
put.description: Called by the worker itself, from its `page` skill, and by approval-service for the worker whose change it took or shipped. `waiting` says the worker needs the person; it stands until the person messages it. `working` only says what it is doing: whether it reads `working` or `idle` is its host's turns. `review` says its change is submitted to approval-service and `done` that it finished, or its change shipped; each needs no live session. Not sent to its host. Once the worker is in `review` or `done` and no turn or background task of its runs, `whenDone` is carried out: `stop` stops its session, and `retire` retires it once `done` (in `review` it is stopped, never retired, so a send-back reaches it).
